## Annotations as fragments

````markdown
```r
library(dplyr)                          # <1>
starwars |>                             # <2>
  filter(species == "Droid") |>         # <3>
  select(name, height, mass)            # <4>
```

1. Load the package.
2. Start from the dataset.
3. Keep the droids.
4. Keep three columns.
````

Each annotation is a fragment, so the arrow keys reveal them one at a time with their tooltips.

## With line highlighting

````markdown
```{.r code-line-numbers="1|2-3|4"}
library(dplyr)                          # <1>
starwars |>                             # <2>
  filter(species == "Droid") |>         # <3>
  select(name, height, mass)            # <4>
```
````

The annotations follow the highlighted lines, so one press moves the highlight and shows the note that goes with it.

## Choosing when each appears

````markdown
```{.r codefrag-annotations="2,4,6"}
```
````

The annotations then appear at fragment indices two, four, and six rather than in sequence, which is how they are interleaved with other fragments on the slide.

````markdown
```{.r code-line-numbers="1|2|3" codefrag-lines="0,2,4,6"}
```
````

`codefrag-lines` does the same for the highlight steps, counting the unhighlighted code as step zero.

A token that is not a number writes a console warning and leaves that slot alone.

## The tooltip overflow fix

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    codefrag:
      patch-tooltip-overflow: true
```

A tooltip inside a scrolling or clipped container is cut off.
The plugin moves it to an ancestor that does not clip, usually the slide, which is on by default.

## A callback

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <script>
          window.codefragOnAnnotationShown = function (context) {
            console.log(context.targetAnnotation);
          };
        </script>
```

YAML cannot hold a function, so the callback is given in HTML.
It receives the anchor, the slide, the target cell, the target annotation, and the tippy instance.
